judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on the Master Servicer's own 'judgment' and on what it 'deems appropriate', and permits reliance on an Officer's Certificate without further inquiry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out for Wells Fargo as Servicer aligns with Section 4.03(b)-(c), which route Wells Fargo terminations through the Trustee instead.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enforcement standard — such extent and time as the Master Servicer 'in its good faith business judgment, would require were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans' — is an elastic hypothetical-owner test, and the last sentence's 'Successor master Servicer' is inconsistently capitalised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final sentence conditions the Trustee's assumption of duties on the Trustee 'not been able to find a successor servicer or a Successor master Servicer', which sits awkwardly with the mandatory termination duties earlier in the same subsection and with Section 8.07.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two long parallel reimbursement regimes, each with an 'including, without limitation' list; the trigger 'not fully and timely reimbursed' has no stated deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reimbursement comes from the Distribution Account, and the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions deduct 'amounts required to be reimbursed pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.03' without mentioning this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short sentence imposing a plain duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.03(b) and the Remittance Date definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence; clear in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.03(b)'s contemplation that the Master Servicer may act as servicer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The required coverage is only 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees' — an undefined market standard with no floor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision fixes a coverage amount or gives anyone the right to approve the bond, so the standard is left entirely at large in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Combines an open grant ('any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable, including but not limited to') with four enumerated powers, a classic general-versus-specific tension, and the REMIC proviso turns on what is 'reasonably within its control'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The grant is made 'subject to the REMIC Provisions and the provisions of Article XI hereof', but Article XI is Termination, which has nothing to do with master servicing powers — the cross-reference does not fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, if heavily qualified by 'to the extent provided in this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers wholesale to the Servicing Agreements, which are exhibits rather than operative text here; no internal conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and mechanical, with an electronic-signature accommodation; the parenthetical '(or if the related Servicer does not, the Master Servicer may)' makes the backstop permissive rather than mandatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Request for Release definition and Exhibit G.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to 'Such trust receipt' although no trust receipt has been mentioned — only a request for release — so the antecedent is missing, and the final clause releases the file on liquidation rather than requiring its return.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Request for Release definition and Section 4.07(a) use a certification, not a trust receipt, so the term has no referent elsewhere in the Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The access sentence is garbled — 'The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access ... to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — leaving it unclear who is entitled to access.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.01 contains a parallel access provision with a different list of grantees and an express Mortgagor-privacy proviso that this subsection lacks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso reads 'the Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall be entitled to setoff', omitting a conjunction, and it declares the funds 'the sole and exclusive property of the Trustee' while simultaneously allowing another party to set off against them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The setoff right must be squared with Section 4.14's compensation scheme and the Servicing Fee definition, and with Section 4.08(a)'s parallel statement that funds are held subject to withdrawals from the Distribution Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Heavily qualified by deference to the Servicing Agreements, and the eligibility requirements are said to be 'set forth in this Agreement' although no such requirements appear in the supplied text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The insurer eligibility requirements it invokes are not in this Agreement; the only comparable standard is the Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac test in the LPMI Policy definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanical in substance but the deposit and withdrawal rules are expressed entirely by section cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites Sections 5.01 and 5.04 for deposits and Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04 for withdrawals, but Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex provision, so the references do not fit the Distribution Account machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear allocation of claim-presentment duties with a workable exception for repair-and-restoration amounts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.09(b) and the Insurance Proceeds definition's carve-out for restoration amounts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Best reasonable efforts' is an internally inconsistent hybrid standard, and the parenthetical 'to the extent that the Mortgage Loan requires the Mortgagor to maintain such insurance' sits oddly with LPMI Policies, which the Servicer pays for.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The LPMI Policy definition makes the Servicer responsible for the premium, which contradicts the assumption in this subsection that the Mortgagor maintains the insurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Otherwise mechanical; the substance is a deposit obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deposits amounts 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05', but Article V of this Agreement ends at Section 5.04 and there is no Section 5.05.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite custody obligations, though 'to the extent available' softens the first sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.02's custodial certification scheme and the Mortgage File definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As to which no satisfactory arrangements can be made for collection of delinquent payments' is a judgment-laden trigger with no decision-maker named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.15 on REO Property and the Liquidated Loan definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward in structure; entitles the Master Servicer to its fee plus float income and offsets Compensating Interest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants float income separately, but the Master Servicing Fee definition already includes 'any amounts earned on permitted investments in the Distribution Account during the Master Servicer Float Period', and the Master Servicing Compensation definition adds it a third time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As expeditiously as possible' is an elastic timing standard, though the REMIC foreclosure-property constraints are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.02's REMIC covenants and the REO Property definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Protected Account definition and Section 4.15(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso refers to 'any such unreimbursed Monthly Advances', a term the Agreement never defines and which does not match the 'Advances' referred to in the same sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term is 'Advance'; the mismatch means the proviso's scope relative to the main clause cannot be settled from the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanically drafted, but the phrase 'net of any payment to the Master Servicer and the related Servicer as provided above' lacks punctuation and the antecedent 'as provided above' spans two subsections.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It keys deposits to 'the Determination Date', of which the definition supplies two different dates depending on the Servicer, and to 'the related Distribution Account', a term not used elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deems any non-compliance, however immaterial, an automatic Event of Default with mandatory immediate termination, and then declares 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That supersession sentence competes with the identically worded sentences in Sections 4.17 and 4.18(b) and with the Event of Default and cure machinery in Article IX, and the Event of Default definition points only to Section 9.01.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and detailed, but it likewise converts any timing failure into an automatic Event of Default and contains its own 'shall supersede any other provision' sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and competes with the supersession and termination sentences in Sections 4.16 and 4.18(b), each drafted slightly differently, so the three cannot all be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An intricate web of deadlines ('within two Business Days after receipt of such copy, but no later than the 12th calendar day after the Distribution Date (provided that, the Securities Administrator forwards a copy ... no later than the 10th calendar day)') that can conflict on particular calendars.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on 'the representations in Section 2.04(vi)' and on Exhibit O to allocate reporting responsibility, both of which exist, and on Section 4.18(a)(vi)(B), a subsection that does not appear in the Agreement's Section 4.18 as drafted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The timing is internally circular: the Master Servicer must sign by the 3rd Business Day after the Reportable Event while the Depositor's approval is also due by the close of business on the 3rd Business Day, and the clause labels '(i)' and '(i)' are duplicated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It again cross-refers to 'Section 4.18(a)(vi)(B)', which does not exist in the Agreement's Section 4.18.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extremely long with nested roman-numeral items, and it describes the Sarbanes-Oxley Certification as being 'described in Section 4.18(a)(ii)(D)' when the certification is in fact set out in subsection (iii)(D) of the same provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also refers to duties 'under Sections 4.18(a)(iv) and (v)' for Form 10-K preparation and to Section 4.18(a)(vi)(B), and uses the capitalised term 'Affiliates', which the Agreement does not define.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence is broken — 'Additional Form 10-D Disclosure, Additional Form 10- Disclosure or any Form 8-K Disclosure Information (collectively, the obligation to include such Additional Information is subject to receipt ...' — so the collective definition of 'Additional Disclosure' is never actually made, and the notification sentence has the same four parties notifying themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definitions section defines 'Additional Disclosure' as 'As defined in Section 4.18', but this is the only place it purports to be defined, so the defined term has no content anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and mechanical; the catch-all trigger 'or for any other reason' is broad but sensible in context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its final sentence says the Securities Administrator's Section 4.18 fees 'shall not be reimbursable from the Trust Fund', while Sections 4.18(a)(i)-(iii) repeatedly make the Depositor responsible for those same fees — reconcilable, but the two provisions pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Depositor and the Master Servicer and each of its officers' uses a singular possessive for two indemnitees, an ambiguity the second paragraph fixes by using 'their respective'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Securities Administrator Information definition points here, and this indemnity runs alongside the general indemnity in Section 8.05, which is outside the supplied text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same singular/plural possessive slip, and the Depositor Information limb is narrowed to information 'that is required to be filed', a qualifier absent from the first paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Securities Administrator and Master Servicer indemnities, but each is scoped slightly differently, so the three are not symmetrical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same possessive slip; the second paragraph runs only in favour of the Depositor while the first also covers the Securities Administrator, an asymmetry within one provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That asymmetry differs from the Securities Administrator's indemnity, which covers both counterparties in both paragraphs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contribution 'in such proportion as is appropriate to reflect the relative fault and the relative benefit of the respective parties' supplies no method for weighing fault against benefit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes 'the defaulting party', a concept the surrounding indemnities do not use; the defined term 'Defaulting Party' relates only to the Swap Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the indemnity paragraphs it preserves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It makes any non-compliance an automatic Event of Default with mandatory termination and then, in its last sentence, says no Event of Default occurs where the failure results from another party's late information — the two statements pull against each other within the same provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'termination ... pursuant to this Section 4.18(d)', but this text sits in Section 4.18(b) and Section 4.18(d) is the e-mail notice provision; it also carries a third 'shall supersede any other provision' sentence competing with Sections 4.16 and 4.17.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence, clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides Section 12.01, the Agreement's amendment provision, permitting amendment of a whole section without Certificateholder consent — the same override technique used in the Eligible Account definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive ('may be delivered') and specifies a single e-mail address and telephone number, which will not survive changes of personnel.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.05 is the Agreement's notices provision, and this subsection creates an alternative channel for a whole category of notices without reconciling the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b) says the parties' obligations 'will be supplemented and modified as necessary to be consistent with any such amendments, interpretive advice or guidance, convention or consensus among active participants in the asset-backed securities markets, advice of counsel, or otherwise' — an open-ended, unbounded modification standard with no named decision-maker.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (d) declares that 'no amendment of this Agreement shall be required' to effect such changes, which cannot be squared with Section 12.01's amendment machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence with an odd trigger — filings 'required by any change in the Uniform Commercial Code' — which says nothing about the initial filings or about continuation statements required by the passage of time.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.01 effects the conveyance and Section 12.02 addresses recordation, but nothing else in the Agreement imposes an initial UCC filing obligation, leaving perfection largely unaddressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The option is given to 'Saxon or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder', yet the third sentence says 'This right may be assigned by the Seller to a third party' — the Seller is not the holder of the right, so the assignment sentence does not fit the grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Purchase Price definition describes this option as belonging to 'the applicable Servicer or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder', which is broader than the Saxon-only grant here, and the Principal Funds definition attributes Section 4.21 repurchases to 'the related Originator, Saxon (or its assignee) or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dense but mostly definite; the sentence requiring the Majority Class CE Certificateholder to fund investment losses 'out of its own funds immediately as realized' is an unusual obligation on a certificateholder.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says investment instructions go to the Securities Administrator and that the Securities Administrator remits swap amounts, while the Swap Account definition makes the Swap Administrator the party that creates and maintains that account; the Supplemental Interest Trust definition also excludes these assets from the Trust Fund even though the Trust Fund definition includes Swap Administration Agreement rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly mechanical, but the sixth sentence directs remission 'in the manner provided in clause (d) below' while the closing sentence refers to payments 'pursuant to clause (d) or clause (e) below', and the deemed-payment sentence uses 'the second preceding sentence' as its anchor, which is fragile drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is what actually establishes the Reserve Fund and requires the Reserve Fund Deposit, yet both the Reserve Fund and Reserve Fund Deposit definitions say they are created and deposited 'pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof', which is the Class P Certificate Account provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two very long nested parentheticals repeat the same exclusion verbatim and the final sentence is cut off mid-phrase ('to the Holders of the Class A, Class M and Class'), leaving the subordination rule incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deducts swap payments from Interest Funds and then Principal Funds, which matches the corresponding limbs of the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions; the deemed-payment ordering also matches the Class IO Distribution Amount definition's 'for purposes of clarity' gloss.
